_comment: Every path in a public skill repo belongs to exactly one class (Skill Repo Spec v1 s9).
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, reference docs, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = tests and examples. Public, SYNTHETIC, produced by tools/make_fixtures.py.
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never git-tracked; lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. The repo ships only the schema.
The line here is subtle and worth stating: metrics/ holds BOTH classes.
history.jsonl / sweep-*.json / doc-drift-cache.json  -> TOOL. They measure the SKILL
(domain counts, source-catalog diffs, a README hash). No real run is described.
live-runs.jsonl                                      -> DATA. It is one line per source
touched during a REAL research run, so it is a record of what the operator was
actually investigating. Tool knowledge distilled FROM it (which source works, which
route falls back) is published -- that is what reference/tools/*.md already is. The
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py, in .githooks and in CI.
`tool` is not a fourth class. It is the per-path allowlist for check 4, which fails any tracked
file that WEARS the shape of real-run output (a jsonl under metrics/, a runs/ tree, a dated file
under an output dir, a live-ledger filename, a database). TOOL is the default class and needs no
entry -- except exactly here, where a TOOL file is shaped like a ledger and has to be argued for
in the diff rather than in a paragraph.
_tool_note: One row per REFRESH PERIOD, not per run: domain/source counts and the free-route share, keyed by period and git sha. It measures the catalog, it names no subject and no query, and reference/tools/*.md is generated from it. It matches the check-4 metrics-ledger shape only because it is a jsonl under metrics/, which is precisely the shape the sibling DATA ledger has -- so it is enumerated instead of exempted by category.
_sealed_note: The repo-root ledger is the ledger's OLD home (11 entries, 2026-06-02..03). Nothing writes there any more -- both the reader (tools/feedback-bump.py) and the writer (tools/incident_helper.py) resolve through tools/datadir.py. It is declared sealed rather than deleted-and-forgotten so that re-adding it is a hard failure, not a quiet regression: .gitignore alone is advisory and `git add -f` walks straight through it.
